271: When someone with a deceitful mind pretends to live a holy life, the five elements (earth, water, fire, air and sky) that make up their own body laugh at them from inside.
272: What good is looking as holy as the sky is high, if your own heart knows the wrong you have done?
282: Even thinking in your mind, “I will sneakily steal what belongs to someone else,” is wrong.
283: What is gained by stealing may seem to grow beyond all limits, but it will all be lost.
286: People with a deep-rooted desire for stealing cannot live within proper limits.
287: Stealing is a dark, sneaky skill. People who have chosen the strength of living within proper limits do not have it.
288: Goodness stays firmly in the hearts of people who know proper limits. In the same way, sneaky deceit stays in the hearts of people who know stealing.
289: People who know nothing but stealing will be destroyed right there, while doing things that go beyond proper limits.
299: Not every lamp is a real lamp. For people of good character, the lamp of truthfulness is the only real lamp.
302: Anger at people stronger than you, where it can do nothing, is bad. Anger at people weaker than you, where it can do harm, is worse than anything else.
312: Even when someone hurts them out of anger, people with pure minds make it their rule not to hurt that person back.
322: Sharing your food with others and protecting all kinds of living things is the greatest of all the good deeds that writers of books on right living have listed.
328: Even if killing brings a gain that is great and seems good, people of good character see any gain that comes from killing as the lowest of things.
330: People say that those who now live poor, miserable lives in sick bodies are the ones who once took the lives of other beings.
343: You must conquer your five senses and, at the same time, give up everything you desire.
361: People say that desire is the seed that, for every living being and at all times, never fails to cause one birth after another.
366: Being afraid of desire is itself goodness, because it is desire that tricks a person.
381: A ruler who has all six parts of a strong country (an army, loyal people, plenty of food and money, ministers, friendly allies and strong forts) is like a lion among kings.
389: The whole world will live safely under the royal umbrella (the sign of his rule) of a king with the good character to put up with words that are bitter to hear.
392: What we call numbers and what we call letters are said to be the two eyes of every living person.
395: People who learn by standing humbly before their teachers, like the poor before the rich, are truly great. Those who do not learn are the lowest of all.
